scope: Behavioral evaluation of existing examples and private-library workflows; not a fresh-agent generation benchmark.

preview.note: Existing persistent preview retained. Installed exact remote CI artifact and source snapshot without changing either active branch. Snapshot must remain while preview uses it.

cases.prompt: Show how type size, line length, leading, and margins change an interface's typography.
cases.basis: Your request for a product-design instrument closer to Anatomy.
steps: Open the typography press.
Choose Reading view.
Use the keyboard to set line length to 26 ch.
Compare the new type bed with the last printed proof.
expected: Real text wrapping changes with the controls.
Leading equals type size multiplied by the leading value.
The last proof is unchanged until Print.

cases.prompt: Print this composition, then keep my draft and last proof when I return.
cases.basis: Persistent interactive lessons inside the private Playgrounds library.
steps: Print the 18 px / 26 ch composition and wait for the complete cycle.
Reload and verify the printed proof.
Change size to 19 px and immediately reload.
Repeat the edit, wait 700 ms, then reload without printing.
expected: Printing commits the draft and completes its cycle.
Both printed and unprinted state survive returning.
All status labels agree with the restored state.

after700ms.stageLabel: Press ready · type and proof match
after700ms.draftLabel: Type is set. Print to see this composition.

issues: A reload before the save debounce completes loses the latest edit.
Initial restoration of a dirty draft shows a false matching-proof status.

cases.prompt: Let me feel the difference between gentle and bouncy interface motion.
cases.basis: Your selected interface motion rig example.
steps: Run Gentle and observe a full cycle.
Run Bouncy and observe a full cycle.
Read the live drawer transform over time and compare the trace.
expected: Gentle settles without overshoot.
Bouncy passes the target then settles.
The drawing, interface drawer, and readouts agree.

cases.prompt: Close the drawer while it is opening, then drag it yourself.
cases.basis: A product-design lesson about responsive, interruptible motion.
steps: Start Bouncy, then click Close during the opening.
Observe position continuity and continued momentum.
Drag the carriage halfway and release.
Use Home and End on the focused rig.
expected: Changing destination does not teleport the drawer or discard its momentum.
Rig and interface move together when dragged.
Keyboard controls change the target.

cases.prompt: Set spring stiffness to 1000, damping to -4, and the target halfway open.
cases.basis: Playgrounds exposed actions let an agent demonstrate the same instrument the user controls.
steps: Call the open rig's set action through the plugin CLI.
Read the returned state and rendered controls.
Call the Gentle preset through the same action interface.
expected: Out-of-range input is normalized.
Agent state matches visible controls.
Named presets use the same runtime as clicks.

cases.prompt: Save this for myself, rename it, and bring it back with my saved inputs.
cases.basis: Your explicit decision to have a private library with independent reused copies.
steps: Save the existing six-person calculator to a new library item.
Set the saved copy to eight people.
Rename it in the UI, navigate to the library, and reopen it.
Publish the saved item into a thread without that playground.
Change that thread's copy to four people and verify the saved item remains eight.
Publish the saved item back into the original six-person thread.
expected: Saved inputs and title survive reopening.
New thread copies are independent.
Reusing a saved item shows its saved inputs, including in the original thread.
issues: Publishing a saved playground into a thread that already owns the same playground ID leaves the thread's old inputs in place.

cases.prompt: Let me use both design instruments on a narrow screen and with reduced motion.
cases.basis: The instruments are embedded in bb and should remain usable across its supported layouts.
steps: Use 390 x 844 CSS px and System dark theme.
Exercise keyboard controls.
Print a 64 ch wide proof and verify only the proof bench scrolls horizontally.
Exercise reduced-motion Close then Open on the served motion frame.
Print a Compact card with reduced motion.
expected: The page fits horizontally.
Keyboard interaction works.
Reduced motion reaches the requested resting state without animation or trace.
cases.methodNote: Reduced-motion emulation was applied to the actual served frame URL in a second page in the same Browser Automation session because parent-page emulation does not propagate to this opaque OOPIF. The frame's own UI was exercised. No mocked bridge or code substitution.

cases.prompt: Make this an Anatomy-based playground and credit the creator.
cases.basis: Your original request to credit Ryan and combine the interactive-learning inspiration.
steps: Inspect the visible creator footer in both instruments.
Verify its links and the inline MIT notice.
Inspect the actual frame sandbox and resource entries.
expected: Ryan's drawing kit is visibly credited.
The Bugged Dev is credited for inspiration.
Ryan's MIT notice remains in the distributed HTML.
The figure runs using inline resources in the existing frame sandbox.
